title: A new company signs up and a user finds the company by e-mail: the public answers and refusals (no company is created)
description: No sign-in is used (actor anonymous). The file works whatever the two switches say, and says which half it ran. QA on 2026-11-26 answers the standard 404 for /api/signup/* and for /api/login-discovery (read from the live answers of GET /api/signup/config and POST /api/login-discovery): the OFF steps then run (the slug check, the verification and the status answer 404 'Not Found') and the ON steps are SKIPPED with the note 'requires signup_on'. When the sign-up is on, the ON steps run instead: the slug check says invalid, reserved or available, and a verification or a status read with an unknown, a too-short or a missing token gets the ONE generic 400 'invalid_or_expired_link' (identical answers, nothing consumed). The e-mail lookup (POST /api/login-discovery) has its own switch: with a well-formed unknown address it answers the neutral 202 'accepted' (on) or 404 (off, the state of QA); a malformed address gets the same neutral 202 (on) or 404 (off). Steps s13 and s14 are skipped on QA with 'requires discovery_on'. A PASS therefore says which half ran: read the skipped notes. NOT automated here: the submit of a real request (POST /api/signup, it records a request and mails a link; the whole path with the mail trap is the file BP-PLATFORM-02-self-service-signup, T-2749) and the 200 'single match' answer of the lookup (it needs a company whose login directory holds a known address; covered by test/letflow/routers/login_discovery_test.exs). The 429 limits (per address, per domain) are not driven: the runner may not saturate a public limiter. Nothing is created, so there is no cleanup and no residue.

steps.says: Anyone reads the public sign-up configuration. 200 when the sign-up is switched on; 404 (the standard answer of a disabled mount) when it is off, which is the state of QA on 2026-11-26. The terms version is remembered only when it is on.
SIGN-UP OFF: the live slug check answers the same standard 404.
SIGN-UP OFF: a verification with any token answers the standard 404 (nothing is looked up).
SIGN-UP OFF: the status of a request answers the standard 404.
SIGN-UP ON: a slug in capital letters and a symbol is reported 'invalid'.
SIGN-UP ON: a slug the platform keeps for itself is reported 'reserved'.
SIGN-UP ON: a slug nobody holds is reported 'available'.
SIGN-UP ON: a verification with a token that never existed gets the one generic 400.
SIGN-UP ON: a token that is too short gets the very same answer.
SIGN-UP ON: no token at all gets the very same answer.
SIGN-UP ON: the status of a request with an unknown token gets the same generic 400.
E-MAIL LOOKUP: a well-formed address that no company knows. 202 'accepted' (neutral) when the lookup is switched on; 404 when it is off. Remembered only when on.
E-MAIL LOOKUP ON: a malformed address (a number instead of text) gets the same neutral 202, never 400, 415, 422 or 500.
E-MAIL LOOKUP ON: an empty body object gets the same neutral 202.
E-MAIL LOOKUP OFF: the same malformed request gets the standard 404, before anything is read.
